originalTitle: US Open 2026: Auger-Aliassime and Musetti depart; Fritz, Osaka and Swiatek win – as it happened
summary: Auger-Aliassime lost in the second round, as did Musetti against Australia’s Dane Sweeny, but Fritz, Swiatek and Andreeva won in straight sets and Osaka survived in three
content: Jovic is up next on Stadium 17, against Fran Jones, the only British player left in the singles, but it’s time to wrap up this blog now, on a day when Taylor Fritz, Iga Swiatek, Naomi Osaka, Amanda Anisimova, Alexandra Eala, Flavio Cobolli, Jakub Mensik and Madison Keys (just) all won, but Felix Auger-Aliassime, Lorenzo Musetti and Britain’s Harriet Dart departed. Do check the site later for a match report on De Minaur (he trails Van de Zandschulp by a break in the first set), while Coco Gauff, Alexander Zverev, Elena Rybakina and Gael Monfils are coming up in the night session. Bye! Andreeva hits long on the match point … and another double fault hands Lys a break point … but Andreeva, with Seal sitting in her box (not sure what the connection is there) saves it, has another match point, fends off another break point, has a third match point (they’ve saved the biggest drama for last) … and the fifth seed takes it with a loopy cross-court forehand winner! She’ll play the Austrian Anastasia Potapova in the third round and, despite being in a tough quarter of the draw that includes Coco Gauff, Amanda Anisimova and Iva Jovic, she looks to be right in the mix. Having trailed 2-0 in the second set, Andreeva is accelerating to victory, winning five games on the spin, and she’s serving for the match at 6-0, 5-2. Andreeva double faults for 15-all and Lys lasers a forehand winner down the line for 15-30! Lys has got Andreeva on the ropes on the next point too, but flaps at a smash and nets. And 30-all turns into 40-30 … From a break down in the second set, Andreeva is now a break up, leading 6-0, 3-2. Alexei Popyrin has followed Tristan Schoolkate out of the tournament, losing 2-6, 7-6, 7-6-2 to Chile’s Alejandro Tabilo, but there was an Australian win earlier, for Dane Sweeny against an out-of-sorts Lorenzo Musetti, and there’s still a strong chance of another, with Alex de Minaur just getting under way against the Dutchman Botic van de Zandschulp. Zheng Qinwen has seen off Yulia Putintseva, 6-4, 2-6, 6-1, and the 2024 Olympic champion, who had to come through qualifying after elbow surgery, will play Madison Keys next. And Zheng will be followed on Court 12, after a women’s doubles match involving the top seeds Siniakova and Townsend, by … Zheng. Michael Zheng, that is, the American wildcard who takes on the lucky loser Bu Yunchaokete, who took out Rafael Jodar in round one. So this is a match of huge opportunity for both players, as they seek to reach the third round of the US Open for the first time. And Lys then breaks for 2-0! How quickly momentum can shift, especially in women’s matches, even though I’m sure Andreeva will prove once more that she has too much much quality for the world No 98. After winning her first grand slam in June, Andreeva has had a fairly subdued summer on the hard courts, but she looked strong in the opening round, and is handed a route back into this second set when Lys serves up no less than three double faults in one game. So it’s Andreeva 6-0, 1-2. They do make a good bagel in New York and Mirra Andreeva has served one up to the poor Eva Lys on Stadium 17. But the biggest cheer of the match comes when Lys finally gets on the board in the opening game of the second set. So Andreeva, the French Open champion, leads the German 6-0, 0-1. Schoolkate is down and quite possibly out, as he falls on the court trying to hit a forehand, giving Cobolli two match points at 40-15. And the Italian seals it with an ace! Having conceded the opening set, Cobolli will be relieved to avoid another five-set match, after his first-round escape act from two sets down. Last year Cobolli faded quickly in the third round after two successive five-setters. He’ll face the winner of Alexander Blockx v Marco Trungelliti in round three this time. Blockx leads 6-3, 6-2, 3-6. Schoolkate smacks away possibly his best shot of the day – it’s not only Cobolli who’s making the highlights reel – but the fine forehand is in vain, as Cobolli sends down a second-serve ace to hold for 5-5. It leaves Cobolli potentially two games from victory, at 3-6, 6-3, 6-4, 5-5, and he’s two points from breaking when Schoolkate’s shot skids just wide for 15-30. Fine margins. Cobolli conjures up an improbable forehand winner – his 40th winner of the day – and it’s 15-40, two break points! And he takes the first with a perfect lob! The fifth seed will serve for the match at 6-5. Speaking of Osaka, here’s Tumaini’s take on her uneven win: For a second consecutive match at the US Open, Naomi Osaka appeared to be cruising. Everything was in hand as the two-time champion established a set and a break lead in her round two match against Katerina Siniakova, an uneventful return to the third round beckoning. Instead of carrying that great momentum forward until the end, though, Osaka was overcome by tension in the final stages of second set and she soon found herself in a decider. It took a significant amount of resilience and restraint for her to reset and find a way through to the third round with a comprehensive final set to win 6-2, 5-7, 6-1. Before the North American hard-court swing, a period that yielded US Open titles in 2018 and 2020, Osaka finally looked like a grand slam contender again. After years of struggling through the clay- and grass-court seasons, seemingly just waiting for the hard courts to return, this year Osaka produced career-best showings on those surfaces to the fourth round at the French Open and quarter-finals at Wimbledon. Her level on grass at Wimbledon, a surface she has toiled on for much of her career, was particularly impressive as she defeated the world No 1, Aryna Sabalenka, in round four. Osaka ran out of steam in the quarter-finals, fatigue seeping in after she reached the Bad Homburg final a week earlier, but it was some of the best tennis she had played since winning her last grand slam title at the Australian Open in 2021. chineseTitle: 2026 年美国公开赛：奥格-阿利亚西姆和穆塞蒂离开；弗里茨、大阪和斯瓦泰克获胜——事实确实如此
chineseSummary: 奥格·阿里亚西姆在第二轮中失利，穆塞蒂也输给了澳大利亚选手戴恩·斯威尼，但弗里茨、斯瓦泰克和安德烈耶娃直落三盘获胜，大阪三连胜
chineseContent: 约维奇接下来将在 17 号体育场对阵弗兰·琼斯，他是单打中唯一剩下的英国选手，但现在是时候结束这篇博客了，这一天泰勒·弗里茨、伊加·斯瓦泰克、娜奥米·大阪、阿曼达·阿尼西莫娃、亚历山德拉·埃拉、弗拉维奥·科博利、雅库布·门西克和麦迪逊·凯斯（刚刚）都获胜，但菲利克斯·奥格-阿利亚西姆、洛伦佐·穆塞蒂和英国的哈里特达特离开了。请稍后查看该网站，了解德米纳尔的比赛报告（他在第一盘中以破发落后范德赞德舒尔普），而可可·高夫、亚历山大·兹维列夫、埃琳娜·雷巴基娜和盖尔·蒙菲尔斯将在夜间比赛中出场。再见！安德烈耶娃在赛点上击出长距离……而另一个双误给了莱斯一个破发点……但是安德烈耶娃，海尔坐在她的盒子里（不确定其中有什么联系）挽救了它，又获得了另一个赛点，抵御了另一个破发点，获得了第三个赛点（他们把最大的戏剧性事件留到了最后）……五号种子凭借一记疯狂的跨场正手制胜球赢得了比赛！她将在第三轮对阵奥地利选手阿纳斯塔西娅·波塔波娃（Anastasia Potapova），尽管在与可可·高夫（Coco Gauff）、阿曼达·阿尼西莫娃（Amanda Anisimova）和伊娃·约维奇（Iva Jovic）等人的抽签中处于艰难的四分之一，但她看起来是正确的组合。在第二盘0-2落后的情况下，安德烈耶娃正在加速取得胜利，在旋转中连赢五局，她的发球局以6-0和5-2领先。安德烈耶娃双误连得15平，而莱斯则以正手制胜，以15-30领先！莱斯在下一分也让安德烈娃陷入困境，但在一次扣杀和入网时扑了上去。 30-30变成了40-30……从第二盘的破发开始，安德烈耶娃再次破发，以6-0和3-2领先。阿列克谢·波皮林 (Alexei Popyrin) 紧随特里斯坦·斯库凯特 (Tristan Schoolkate) 出局，以 2-6、7-6、7-6-2 输给了智利选手亚历杭德罗·塔比洛 (Alejandro Tabilo)，但早些时候澳大利亚队取得了胜利，戴恩·斯威尼 (Dane Sweeny)
